String: You're being told it's because it's been too long since you produced a single hit.
They're saying you've not demonstrated any talent for producing music in a long time.
They said your lack of ambition is dragging the company's <rep/cred/standing/image> down.

They told you that, at the pace you bring on new clients, they'd rather <eat glass/walk into traffic/throw themselves off a bridge/watch Skibidi Toilet on repeat/listen to Baby Shark on repeat> than keep working with you.
You heard someone say that your musical vibes are <dead/deceased/pushing daisies/lifeless/inert/stone-cold, and not in the cool Steve Austin way>.
You overheard someone ask if you'd just been <hibernating/doing jack-all/living under a rock/coasting/quiet quitting/jacking off> for the last few years.
You heard one of your coworkers call you a <hack/never-has-been/bully/wet blanket/trifler/talentless tinkerer>.
They said to not let the door hit you <on your way out/where the good Lord split you>.
One of your coworkers remarked that your MIDI keyboard is literally gathering dust.
You've been told that you sneezed on the beat, but didn't make it sicker.
A coworker muttered that when you bother to pitch a beat, the sounds are, like, so <num5-10> years ago.
They're saying that <a chimpanzee/a toddler/a drunk in the drunk tank/a lazy sloth/a tortoise/a ninety-year-old grandma/a ninety-year-old grandpa/a zombie> could make songs faster than you.
Someone said they've been using your office as <a break room/a lactation room/an extra bathroom/storage/a secret party room/meditation room>, since you're never there.
One of your coworkers wondered if you'd <died/been kidnapped>, because you're never in the office.
You're told that the latest release of <Ableton Pro/GarageBand/Logic Pro> included you in an "in memoriam" section, as they thought you'd passed.
After not producing anything for so long, an exec wished you good luck in rehabilitating your reputation in the biz.
Someone asked if you'd been in an accident and lost the ability to make music.
You've been told your <procrastination/delay> in making new music is a clear sign that you're no longer interested in producing music.
A coworker asked if you were competing for a world record for longest number of years without producing a single <track/hit/song>.
An exec remarked that you could only coast for so long.
An exec caught wind of a more productive artist on <YouTube/Soundcloud/X>, and doesn't need you anymore.
They said you were taking your job for granted, and that they had enough of your ghosting.
They said you've been MIA and costing them money.
They said it's because your absence is more noticeable than you think, and that if you aren't going to make anything, maybe this wake-up call is what you need to get your life straight.
They said it's because they've seen you deliberately walk past the production building to do other things.
They said they haven't heard a sound from your station for the past two years.

They said that artists have been making up excuses to reach their deadlines without you around, <and they all sound horrible/and they've been producing trash/because they needed someone who could properly foster their talents, and it definitely isn't you>.
They said they haven't seen you in so long, they might as well hire someone more reliable.
They said you were becoming a bottleneck in their operation, and the best solution is to simply cut you out of the equation all together.
An exec at the company said, "You snooze, you lose," as he slammed the door in your face.
After not seeing you for so long, they thought you overdosed <beneath the building/underneath a bridge/somewhere> and forgot the responsibilities you had to fulfill.
